author: Platform Documentation
deck: The document generator behind this platform just got three real upgrades: you can now see what every generation costs, set a hard spending limit, and lock AI-generated images to a consistent brand look.
description: A plain-language rundown of PDF-Tool's latest update: per-job cost receipts, a configurable spending guardrail, and seed/LoRA support for brand-consistent AI imagery -- plus an honest look at what's still catching up.

public.body: Generating a document or an image used to be a bit of a black box: it worked, but you couldn't see what it cost, and nothing stopped a runaway job from quietly running up a bill. AI-generated product photos also tended to drift -- ask for the same kind of image twice and you'd get two different styles. This update fixes all three: every generation now reports what it actually cost, a spending limit catches problems before they get expensive, and images can be locked to a consistent, repeatable brand look.
public.title: Why this update matters

public.body: This builds on ground already covered: PDFs generated here can flow across multiple pages and mix photos, colored panels, dividing lines, and real tables in the site's own colors -- confirmed live and covered in detail in the platform's own downloadable-PDFs article. The catalog attached to this article is a fresh example: seven pages, built entirely from that same pipeline.
public.title: Real documents, not just longer ones

public.body: Every image or PDF job now comes back with a real cost receipt: which provider and model did the work, how the price was calculated, and the estimated cost in dollars. Free, template-only PDF renders get a receipt too -- an honest zero, not silence -- so a per-request total can always be trusted rather than guessed at.
public.title: You can now see what every generation costs

public.body: Each request now runs against a spending ceiling. If a job would push a request's total past that limit, it stops with a clear error instead of running unchecked -- cheap insurance against a stuck loop turning into a real bill. The limit is configurable per site; a sensible default is on by default.
public.title: A spending limit that catches problems before they get expensive

public.body: Two new controls keep AI-generated imagery consistent instead of random. A seed locks in the same visual outcome for the same prompt, so a re-run looks like the same photoshoot rather than a different one. A per-brand style file (a trained LoRA) goes further, locking the look itself -- palette, mood, medium -- across hundreds of generations. The system also now refuses to pair a brand style file with a model that can't actually carry it, so that combination can't silently fall back to an off-brand result. At roughly a tenth of the cost of the general-purpose alternative for the same volume, this is the default path going forward, not a premium option.
public.title: Product photos that actually match your brand

public.body: In the spirit of this site's own documentation standard, here's an honest look at what has and hasn't been proven. Update, same day: the longer, web-page-style PDF path (real HTML and CSS instead of a fixed template) has now been taken all the way through a real validate-and-publish cycle for the first time -- see the rendering-engines deep dive linked below, an 8-page document that is itself the proof. Searching stock photo libraries from directly inside the platform is still fully built behind the scenes but still isn't reachable from here; for now, image generation remains the supported path. Neither gap affects anything described above, which is confirmed working today.
public.title: What's still catching up -- and what just got proven
